newsitem.title: INDIA: India call ends at 10.25-10.75 pct, off day's high.
newsitem.headline: India call ends at 10.25-10.75 pct, off day's high.

text.p: Indian call money ended Thursday in the 10.25-10.75 percent range, down from the day's high of 12.25 percent, dealers said.
Call money stabilised after an initial jump from the day's opening 10.75 percent, they said. Most of the day's deals were around 11 percent, they said.
"There was an initial spurt from 10.75 to 12.25 percent," a dealer at a state-run bank said. "But by late morning, rates had dipped below 11 percent and stabilised in the 10.25-10.75 percent range."
He said rates stabilised as several banks seemed to have availed of export refinance from the central bank.

Banks are allowed to draw refinance from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) against their export credit disbursals at a rate of 11 percent per annum. Dealers said banks had around 45 billion rupees of unavailed refinance limits with the RBI.

Borrowings above 11 percent would have been only from smaller foreign and private banks, he said. "Most state-run banks have export refinance limits with the RBI and it is unlikely they would have borrowed above 11 percent," he said.

Dealers said the tightness in call money rates appeared to be from a combination of factors. A pick-up in credit disbursals by banks, heavy cash withdrawals during local holidays and open market operations by the RBI caused a temporary liquidity crunch, they said.
Dealers however felt rates would come down to around eight percent by the beginning of next week.
"Money withdrawn for spending during the festivals should be back with banks latest by the weekend," said a dealer. "Rates should then ease up."
Security prices fell initially as banks responded to higher call money rates by selling stock, dealers said. But prices recovered later in the day after rates stabilised, they added.
The 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock fell to 102.40 rupees on Thursday from its Wednesday's close of 102.7 before recovering to 102.54 rupees.
The 13.50 percent 1998 stock fell to 102.19 rupee from its last trade price of 103.23 before recovering to 102.59.
